There is higher than usual organic content in the river due to runoff from the spring melt.

Higher organic content = higher chlorine demand = more smell/taste.
It appears that the other 30 km of meewasin  is just not enough to satisfy this guy. Gotta have every inch of the waterfront even though they won’t be using the water themselves.

No one needs you to inform them of incorrect facts though. You said they can’t access the river. Edit your post then. Quit spreading disinformation. Also bikers should stay out of the off leash dog park.

Basement suites in private residence:  Avoid anything with electric baseboard heating. Cheap to install, expensive to operate. Unless it's included in the rent. Which is highly unlikely.

If the car doesn't have a block heater, get one.

[Parking](https://parking.usask.ca/options/student.php) can be difficult on/near campus. Consider locations in close proximity to public transit routes that lead directly to campus. Not that west of the river is necessarily bad, but the bridges are bottlenecks during peak traffic times, or if there is an accident. Living south or east of campus is less problematic in that respect.
That’s because the river is part of the dog park as people have repeatedly pointed out to you and yet you still seem to be ignoring.

>School zone, single lane in either direction with street parking. 

The street parking lane is not a driving lane. Even if there's no one parked there so you can physically drive in it doesn't mean you're allowed to.

I have to make a left hand turn at an intersection on a lower traffic, Meewasin Trail-connected intersection of Spadina quite frequently. While I was waiting to make my turn, a pedestrian started crossing. A vehicle went around me on the right, going into the bike lane, and almost smoked the pedestrian.

What a downright stupid council we elected in this city. Oh, what a great idea, remove the benches so no one can sit down. I already can't park my truck anywhere downtown, so I walk, and now I won't be able to have a seat anywhere that isn't a bar.  How about we remove the sidewalks so no one can lay down, or remove the trails by the river and all the recycling depots to deter encampments. Let's stop all public transport to stop people from sleeping there.  

Seriously, what's next? This laughable waste of resources we call a council needs to pull their incompetent heads out of their dumb asses and actually run the city!

If you don’t like winter , move! I’m so tired of people complaining about winter.  It’s to long of a season to complain about it. By some FN snowshoes, ski, walk the river.  There is no such thing as bad weather, just unsuitable clothing.  Buy a parka.

Sure… when you have a cop nearby who can actually, catch, arrest and charge the person. And its not illegal to be on drugs in public unless you are operating a motor vehicle, causing a disturbance, committing a crime or have drugs on you. I work downtown and even though you see the community officers around 90%+ of the problem is undetected and unmanaged and petty stuff gets them back out onto the street to just repeat the cycle again with no meaningful change. Jail temporarily solves the housing, medical, and food issues for junkies so it is not really much of a punishment, is it?  Right now, some of them are camped out along the river so get ready for when the weather turns and they all come back into the downtown and core areas then there will be a surge again.

I have along with other unauthorized modifications to the dirt trails. Every time they deflect and say the riverbank isn’t theirs and to talk to Meewasin. Meewasin says they don’t have the resources and it goes into a black hole. 

It is ironic because if a homeless person puts up a tent along the river there are unlimited city resources dispatched to get rid of them.

I’m with your mom. I worked downtown in two different locations. Both required me to park and walk a block. Both walks were sketchy. Then some stabbings happened in the area I used to work in and my old coworkers started to be even more scared.

We tried to walk in groups or get from A to B as fast as humanly possible. 

This was 4th ave s and just behind the theatre at River landing with parking by the farmer’s market. 

Early morning and evening outside of normal busy commute times was pretty terrifying. 

At the one lot we had a homeless man who was around a lot. The one time a kind of creepy/ drunk guy was wandering the lot he stayed between him and me and was really kind to try to help me get down the block without issue. Our regulars we were quite ok with. We knew they were just staying warm and minding their business. It was the new people who showed up that were often kind of unsafe acting. 

And honestly shame to the lot for cutting down the trees that wonderful guy was living in. When he moved on it was worse. He wasn’t a problem.

The highest cause of cycling injuries and deaths are getting right hooked- vehicles turning without looking. Riding on the sidewalk is MUCH more dangerous than being in flow which is why it's illegal for adults, and it's kind of gross we put our kids in the place where you're most likely to get killed on two wheels. We need low traffic streets like the 14th bikeway, or completely separate infrastructure like the Meewasin. Bikes don't belong on the sidewalk, they belong where it's safe.
You gate the water line and then choose to open and go out. My friend's dogs died in the river at Sutherland. You should really be advocating for a gate.
Saskatoon has a river. That makes it more dangerous than regina by default /s

12 years ago I would spend all night out until 2am longboarding around river landing and downtown without a soul in sight during the summer. I did this very frequently. This is simply not something that is safe to do anymore. Danger was localized in specific areas of the city once, but now where crime occurs is much less predictable.

It's probably about the worst possible spot for an arena. Blocked access from three sides with everyone having to enter off 20th unless we tear down the first avenue freeway ramp to get access on two sides (but lose all the parking under the ramp by the rremai? Leave the fire department with a single approach in an emergency when 10,000 people are trying to get out or make an opening in the median so people can turn left across the main bridge assuming it isn't backed up across the river?

Two blocks to the nearest hotel instead of two hotels either on the same plot or across the street? Who's going to want to walk past Midtown to get to a hotel after a concert or game? No access to the convention space at TCU which means the city either has to maintain two separate convention spaces two blocks apart for large and small conventions with no ability to expand or shift people from one to the other on an as-needed basis or find even more land to re-locate all the function of TCU place which we still owe money for renovating?

If they need more parking or expansion, do they fill in the river to make room instead of using all the space the city already owns north of 23rd by the existing plan?

Yeah, nah, man. That's not a big deal. Bolt might need a little snugging, but it's nowhere near loose enough to be a problem, unless they've started driving cattle up and down those stairs.
Folks don't remember how bad the old Vic bridge had to get before the city considered it a problem. No chunks of beam falling into the river, no problem.

Over in Brighton we see lots of foxes and rabbits and birds and can hear the coyotes at night. We even had a muskrat at the one smaller pond in previous years. There’s also a family of cobra chickens that raises their babies every year by that same pond, I think this past year there was over 30 babies. Started off with just one breeding pair only a few years ago. Lots of bunnies around. But I also see bunnies on occasion behind my office downtown a few blocks away from the river.

Birds include ducks, canada geese, robins, other songbirds, and the odd crow or raven.

So I work in Toronto and take the TTC every day. I'm used to navigating mentally ill and drug addicted people. I was in downtown Saskatoon earlier this year and I'm telling you it's comparable and possibly worse. I was accosted on two separate occasions in that mall a couple blocks north of the river. It's very unfortunate.

Why should I have to enrol my kids in a swim club for them to go blow off steam after school at the pool. That makes no sense. When these 8-10,00 kids are done their lessons where are they supposed to go swim, the river?

Folks saying avoid "west and the alphabets" are just repeating city mythology that's flatly not true; I know people who have had their homes broken into in Broadway, and Lakeridge in broad daylight, and people in Riversdale who have been there for twenty years without an issue. Meth addicts have legs, they go wherever there's something to steal. There are some lovely affordable places in Caswell Hill, Riversdale, King George, Holiday Park, and you're on tree-lined streets right by the golf course, park, badminton club, river trails, outdoor pool, and rowing club. I half think that people who live there keep the myth going to keep the prices low. The sketchy bits are really Pleasant Hill onwards.

This isn't winter.

Go enjoy some walks before winter really settlies in. Along the river. Maybe checkout the swale area. Check out neighborhood parks. One by wildwood golf course, Hyde park....

I agree with you.  However there has been no action.  This is a “city” that doesn’t care about the big things happening here as everyone runs to the suburbs where they don’t have to look at it.

We did many things during covid that kept people off the streets such as using hotels to house people.  This could be done again.  From a services standpoint it seems that most clinics etc. are in the burbs so then why not utilize these spaces - there are no services at 20th and 3rd for these people, yet they are there.

Not trying to be a flappy but as you say, but I have never lived in a place where the apathy is just so prevalent.  Perhaps we should be looking at different solutions rather than throwing our arms up and saying it is complicated.  

Open air drug markets and use needs to stop - perhaps pick an area where it is allowed and arrest those who use outside of it?  It worked in Vancouver for years before liberal policies destroyed the city.  

Outside of that - how about snow removal?  Why don’t we do that?  If we are forced to have provincial insurance (with astronomical rates) then the municipality has a duty of care to keep the roads safe.  

How about the river?  Why was there not any reaction to not opening the dam - Paris of the Prairies?  Not for long no need for bridges in a few years … let alone  need for a rowing/canoe club.

I think of mindsets here changed to wanting tourism, and money in general we would see something change.  But alas - everyone has an opinion but don’t stay in the city and go to their safe little neighbourhoods where they don’t have to see what is going on … until you find someone in your attic in Varsity View.
Avoid places on the west side of the river other than Dundonald, Kensington and Hampton Village. Avoid Sutherland on the east side.
I think you’ll be ok, just stay together near the river and don’t go downtown in the evenings alone
Time to bring a trained dog to the area to scare them off. There are plenty of spots along the river where we aren't.
